clue.text: Fight follows angry exchange about school head

indicators.note: the angry exchange goes about, around, the letter it takes in

parts.note: cross words are words spoken in anger, a row

indicators.note: the head of school is its first letter

explanation.surface: A scuffle breaks out after a heated row concerning the headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S, the head of 'school', inside CROSS WORDS, splitting it as CROSS S WORDS; 'follows' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords with someone is an idiom for clashing or quarrelling, as duellists once did with blades.

clue.text: The truth is, I invested in property

indicators.note: something invested in another is placed inside it, as money is put into an asset

parts.note: realty is land and buildings, real estate

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that they have put money into real estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality is what actually is so, the plain facts as opposed to fiction.

clue.text: Indignant on seeing evidence of condensation

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross on noticing misted windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up or angry is one sense; windows clouded over with vapour show the other, literal sense.

clue.text: Brown is self-righteous in the main

indicators.note: the sanctimonious word sits inside the word for the ocean

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
pi is informal shorthand for pious, sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A suntanned sailor is smug about life on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown pigment, originally from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: It's instrumental in getting CIA involved with oran

indicators.note: letters involved with one another are tangled up and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Something helps spies become entangled with a mysterious party called Oran.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, so it is literally instrumental.

clue.text: The lady's left to enjoy herself

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, so the lady's is Di's
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A woman has been given leave to go off and have fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To disport oneself is to frolic or amuse oneself.

clue.text: Decline to offer it to a girl

parts.note: to give is to offer or hand over
taken as written
a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to hand something over to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something or choose not to attend is an idiomatic way of saying no to it.

clue.text: Openings to get in new subscribers

indicators.note: the letter gets in, entering the openings

parts.note: doors are openings into a building

explanation.surface: Gaps are needed to bring fresh paying members into a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Donors are contributors who give money, as subscribers to a fund or charity do.

clue.text: Separate from one so unpunctual

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
late means not on time

explanation.surface: Someone is kept apart from a habitual latecomer.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to set apart or cut off from others, a verb meaning to separate.

clue.text: Quiet recruit wins commendation

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
to raise troops is to recruit them

explanation.surface: A shy new soldier is honoured with a citation.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is approval expressed in words, a synonym for commendation.

clue.text: Even grinned inanely and without cessation

indicators.note: inanely means foolishly and senselessly, so the letters are jumbled into nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone smirked foolishly and on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes on forever has no stop or pause.

clue.text: Cockney chap acquired 'is money by self-seeking

parts.note: a Cockney drops the h of he, saying 'e
got means acquired
the Cockney 'is is the word his, written as is

explanation.surface: A London working man got hold of his cash through selfishness.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their h's, so 'he' becomes 'e and 'his' becomes 'is.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotism is excessive concern with oneself, the noun sense of selfishness.

clue.text: Bill and I ask if it's fatty

parts.note: an ad, a poster or advertisement, is a bill
to pose a question is to ask it

explanation.surface: Two people wonder whether some food is high in fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose describes animal tissue that stores fat.

clue.text: Irascible if leaving to give evidence

indicators.note: the little word departs from the longer one, leaving a gap

parts.note: to testify is to give evidence in court
taken as written

explanation.surface: A witness becomes bad-tempered when doubts are dropped from their testimony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes IF out of TESTIFY, giving TESTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy means easily irritated or short-tempered.

clue.text: Amend list in order to do demolition work

indicators.note: putting things in order means rearranging them, so the letters are sorted anew

explanation.surface: A council revises a roster so that a building can be pulled down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order to' reads as a purpose phrase; 'in order' is the anagram signal and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take apart piece by piece, as wreckers do to a structure.

clue.text: Shortly to incorporate a large counter in the snug

indicators.note: one word incorporates others by taking them into its body

parts.note: soon means shortly, before long
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
a bar is the counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: A big serving counter will soon be installed in a cosy pub room.
explanation.walkthrough: A snug and a saloon bar are both rooms in a traditional British pub, the snug small and private, the saloon the more comfortable lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both name a separate, more comfortable room in a British pub, so one stands for the other.

clue.text: Urban centre in Germany Henry left with a friend

indicators.note: the letter has left, gone away from the city's name

parts.note: Munich is a major city in Germany
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
a means one, and one is I in Roman numerals
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A man named Henry departs a German city with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes H from MUNICH to leave MUNIC; 'a' is read as one, the Roman I.
explanation.definitionFit: Municipal means belonging to a town or city and its local government.

clue.text: Objective is to get nature reserve money

indicators.note: read as re-serve, the letters are served up again in another order

parts.note: L stands for pound or lira, units of money

explanation.surface: A conservation charity aims to raise funds for a wildlife sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' is read as re-serve: NATURE rearranged gives NEUTRA, then L for money follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Being neutral means taking no side, which is what impartial or unbiased judgement requires.

clue.text: Bell has a mad fancy

parts.note: a chimer is something that chimes, a bell

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer harbours a crazy whim.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild illusion or impossible dream, a fanciful notion.

clue.text: Many long to find hidden treasure

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Lots of people yearn to dig up buried riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a stash of valuables put away out of sight.

clue.text: Reflective unionists reckon it's a money-saver

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-reversed, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the TUC, Trades Union Congress, is the body of British trade unions
to rate is to reckon or estimate

explanation.surface: Thoughtful trade unionists conclude that something saves cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' turns TUC round to CUT; the TUC is Britain's national federation of trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-rate goods are sold at a discount, so buying them saves cash.

clue.text: Eccentric causes row in Cyprus

indicators.note: the row sits inside the island's code

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
a rank is a row of people or things

explanation.surface: A quarrel in Cyprus is caused by an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranky in this sense means odd or full of strange notions, as a crank is.

clue.text: Looked hard at boss involving cast

indicators.note: the first word involves, wraps round, the second

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob on a surface
a die is a mould used for casting metal

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinised their employer, who was hiring actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Studied means examined closely and carefully.

clue.text: Actions taken by homeowners

explanation.surface: Things done by people who own their houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeds are acts or feats; deeds are also the legal documents proving ownership of a property.

clue.text: Not in charge when travelling from home

parts.note: out means not at home or not in
a ward is someone in another's charge

explanation.surface: A guardian is off duty while on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The outward leg of a trip is the one heading away, as opposed to the return.

clue.text: It's so easy to find brick-making material

explanation.surface: Someone finds that making building blocks is no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Breeze is cinder or coke ash, used in Britain to make light breeze blocks for building.
explanation.definitionFit: Something simple is informally a cinch; cinders and ash mixed with cement form building blocks.

clue.text: Lad grips Harrow to extract fern

indicators.note: the boy's name grips, holds inside it, the word for torment

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name, a lad
to harrow is to torment, as to rack is

explanation.surface: A boy from the famous school takes hold of a plant to pull it up.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school, so 'Harrow' with its capital looks like a place, but here it is the verb to torment.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracken is a large coarse fern that covers heaths and hillsides.

clue.text: Last soldier may be incompatible

indicators.note: may be signals that the letters could be formed into something else

explanation.surface: The final infantryman in line might not fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-assorted things are badly matched and do not go together.
